Continuity of a function, types of discontinuity, graphs of discontinuous function

Rules of differentiation; derivatives of parametric and implicit functions; higher order derivatives

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Area between two curves is |f − g| made structured: the intersections supply the limits and split points, the strip test fixes who is on top, and top-minus-bottom integrates the resolved order. Interior crossings swap the roles and demand partitioning; the slicing axis is chosen by counting splits; and verified symmetry doubles a half.…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Integrating one curve and ignoring the other instead of taking the difference.  ·  Using the same expression over the whole interval when the top curve changes partway.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Where a formula is quoted it is valid only under the conditions stated; Integrating one curve and ignoring the other instead of taking the difference.  ·  Every result here follows from the definitions, so a first-principles derivation is always a valid fallback in the exam.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The swap*** - two curves crossing mid-interval: the strip test (who is on top at a sample point?) settles each subinterval's order.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Failing to find the intersection points, which is what actually bounds the region.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Work through the authored practice problems and re-derive each key formula from the definition.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Solve f = g first; the intersection x-values are the integral's limits and split points.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (6m): Find the area of the region bounded by y = x² and y = x.** — **Intersections:** x² = x ⟹ x = 0, 1 ⟹ limits [0, 1]. **Order test:** at x = 1/2: line 1/2 > parabola 1/4 ⟹ **line on top**. **Evaluate:** ∫₀¹(x − x²)dx = [x²/2 − x³/3]₀¹ = 1/2 − 1/3 = **1/6**.…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): Find the area between y = 4 − x² and y = x + 2.** — **Intersections:** 4 − x² = x + 2 ⟹ x² + x − 2 = 0 ⟹ (x + 2)(x − 1) = 0 ⟹ x = −2, 1. **Order test:** at x = 0: parabola 4 > line 2 ⟹ parabola on top throughout (no interior crossing).…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Negative answers mean the order was wrong on some strip - re-test with a sample point.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Top-minus-bottom is |f - g| disassembled: the intersection analysis resolves the absolute value into an explicit order.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Area between curves = integral of (top - bottom) dx, nonnegative; intersections from f = g supply the limits and any splits. Interior crossings swap top/bottom - partition and test one point per strip. The formula is |f - g| with the absolute value resolved by the order analysis.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The slicing axis is a computational decision: count the splits each choice demands.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (6m): Find the area of the region bounded by x = y² and x = 4.** — **Set-up choice:** the boundaries are x = y² (left) and x = 4 (right) — functions of y ⟹ **horizontal slices (dy)**. **Intersections:** y² = 4 ⟹ y = ±2 ⟹ limits y ∈ [−2, 2].…  ·  **NEB-style (6m): Find the area enclosed between y² = 2x and y = x − 4 — carefully identifying all boundary pieces.** — **Intersections:** substitute x = y + 4 into y² = 2x: y² = 2y + 8 ⟹ y² − 2y − 8 = 0 ⟹ (y − 4)(y + 2) = 0 ⟹ y = 4, −2 ⟹ points (8, 4) and (2, −2).…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Companion Doorway to Area Between Two Curves This canonical is the **short-form doorway** to area between two curves: the top-minus-bottom integral, intersection finding, and the split protocol in one page.…  ·  ## 2. Theorem Mirror - **Basic formula:** area = ∫ₐᵇ[top − bottom]dx where top is the larger y on each strip — always nonnegative. - **Intersections:** solve f(x) = g(x) to find a and b (and any interior crossings that force splits). - **Split protocol:** if the curves cross inside [a, b], the top/bottom roles swap — partition at each crossing and sum the pieces.…  ·  ## 3. Deep Conceptual — Top Minus Bottom Is |Difference| Made Structured - The area between curves is ∫|f − g|dx in principle; the **top-minus-bottom form is that absolute value resolved by knowledge of which curve is on top** — the intersection analysis converts |·| into an explicit order. Finding intersections is not bookkeeping; it is the absolute value's disassembly.…

rows.text: Find the area between y = 4 − x² and y = x + 2.  ·  Find the area between x = y² and x = 4.  ·  ## 4. Deep Conceptual — Choosing the Slicing Axis - **Vertical slices (dx)** suit curves given as y = f(x); **horizontal slices (dy)** suit curves given as x = g(y) or regions bounded left-right by functions of y. The choice that avoids splitting is the cheaper computation.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 5. Worked Example Types - **Type A — no interior crossing:** one integral, top minus bottom. - **Type B — interior crossing:** split at the crossing, two integrals. - **Type C — dy slicing:** horizontal strips for x = g(y) boundaries. - **Type D — symmetric doubling:** verify symmetry, compute half, double.  ·  ## 6. Common Confusions **"Top minus bottom needs absolute values":** once the order is known per strip, plain subtraction is correct — the |·| was resolved by the analysis. **"Integrate in dx always":** count the splits; dy may halve the work.
